title: Metric translation and trace anchors - ops brief
content:
Purpose:
This brief sketches a compact pattern for translating product-level metrics (customer facing) into operator dashboards and trace anchor points for rapid investigation. The aim is to reduce cognitive load for oncall engineers by providing a narrow, high-signal surface: one landing panel per major failure class, with 3–4 supporting metrics and 2 trace anchors.

Scope and constraints:
- Focus: inference request path (ingest -> routing -> serving runtime -> kv cache -> response). Not covering embeddings/analytics pipelines in full.
- Constraint: dashboards must render within 500ms for operator views (query limits). Keep heavy probes behind a toggle.
- Backwards compatibility: reuse existing metric names where possible; add translation keys for new composite metrics.

Operator landing pad pattern (concept):
- Landing panel (single row): top-line SLI, brief note on expected baseline, immediate next action.
- Supporting mini-panels (3): throughput/call-rate, p50/p95 latency, error-rate (per-type).
- Context strip: recent config/rollout metadata and model-version tag.
- Trace anchors: span ids to jump into a session reconstruction view for the sampled request and the corresponding model host.

Metric translation guidelines (examples):
- Product metric: customer_ttf_user_visible_ms -> Operator SLI: ttf_first_token_ms (instrumentation: time from API gateway receive to first token emission).
  - Translation rule: if gateway-latency > 50ms, annotate gateway as slow and show gateway latency histogram.
- Product metric: generate_completion_cost_units -> Operator metric: token_compute_ms_per_request + kv_cache_hit_ratio.
  - Translation: split cost into compute and cache components to help triage cost spikes.
- Product metric: chat_hallucination_rate (ML quality) -> Operator: ml_quality_alert_indicator (binary) + sample_id link for replay.
  - Note: ML signals live in a separate quality dashboard but include a compact indicator on the ops landing pad with a link to the sample set.

Tracing anchor design:
- Two canonical anchors per landing pad: request-lifecycle (API -> router -> model host) and kv-cache-path (cache lookup -> fallback to model).
- Required span annotations: model_version, route_id, tenant_id, kv_key_hash, request_size_tokens. Keep annotations under 10 fields.
- Sampling: adaptive sampling where error or high-latency responses get 100% sampling for 10 minutes after a spike, otherwise targeted 1% baseline sampling per route.
- Trace retention policy: high-fidelity traces kept 7 days, annotated rollups retained 90 days.

Dashboard wireframe notes (practical panels):
1) Landing row (single-number tiles):
   - SLI: p99 end-to-end latency (last 1h) with delta vs baseline.
   - SLI: error-rate (5m) broken down by error class (timeout, oom, tokenization, guardrail).
   - Cache: kv-warmth-index (fraction of requests hitting cached prefix).
2) Heatmap row: latency distribution by route and model-version (interactive).
3) Time-series row: throughput, compute-ms, kv-hit-rate over last 24h with anomaly overlays.
4) Investigator quicklinks: jump to trace anchor, open recent failing requests table, link to replay harness.

Playbook excerpt (oncall steps):
- Step 0: Check landing row. If p99 latency spike > 2x baseline -> proceed to Step 1.
- Step 1: Check heatmap to isolate route/model-version. Pin time window to spike.
- Step 2: Open request-lifecycle trace anchor for a sampled failing request. Confirm whether router delay, model warmup, or kv fallback.
- Step 3: If cache fallback is dominant, surface kv metrics and warmup countermeasures (increase prefix cache TTL / prewarm).
- Step 4: If model host CPU/GPU saturation identified, trigger scaling policy or failover plan documented in infra-runbook.

Rollout checklist for new landing pad or metric translation:
- [ ] Define product metric -> operator metric mapping and translation rule.
- [ ] Add span annotations to tracing instrumentation and update sampling policy.
- [ ] Create dashboard panels with query budget targets.
- [ ] Link quick actions: trace jump, replay, incident template prefill.
- [ ] Smoke test with synthetic probe (canary) and a small-scale tabletop.

Open questions / follow-ups:
- How do we surface ML-quality regressions without flooding ops? Proposed: gated mini-indicators with severity thresholds and sample links.
- Can we centralize translation rules in a small library so SDKs and dashboard templates share the same mapping? Action: spike (ENG-OBS-PRIORITY).
- Query cost: need an accounting model for panel cost per refresh per operator dashboard (first pass due EOD 2026-03-12).

Notes to self / TODOs:
- Draft a lightweight JSON schema for metric translation rules (fields: product_metric, operator_metric, transform, alert_threshold).
- Coordinate with serving-runtime team to standardize model_version tag (ask Marcus Li).
- Add example queries for Grafana/Lexicoder in next revision.

References and quick links:
- JIRA-OBS-842: landing pad prototype and prototype queries
- Confluence: Telemetry Translation Patterns (linked artifact CONFLUENCE-1234)
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/obs-tooling/pull/210

If you're reading this and want to contribute: leave an inline note with suggested metric name or a sample query. Aim for 1–2 sentence suggestions.

-- Aisha
